title: observability: token-kv tracing + cost/latency dashboard and alert tuning
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: customers and internal SRE teams asked for better visibility into token-level KV cache performance, end-to-end token cost attribution, and tracing hooks to correlate expensive requests with underlying KV behavior. This PR adds a combined token-KV cost/latency dashboard, tracing spans for KV cache ops, and tuned alerts to reduce noise while keeping sensitivity for regressions.

What this change does: adds a Grafana dashboard (token_kv_cost_latency.json) with panels for per-route token cost, token latency p50/p95/p99, cache hit/miss ratios broken down by model and sequence length bucket, and KV operation latency/tracing waterfall. Introduces structured tracing spans in the serving runtime (observability/trace/token_kv_spans.go) that annotate requests with cache decision metadata (prefix hit, kv-hit, kv-miss, cache-ttl). Adds new Prometheus metrics for token_cost_per_route, token_latency_seconds_bucketed, kv_cache_hit_total (labels: model, route, seq_bucket), and kv_operation_duration_seconds. Adds alert tuning in observability/alerts/token_kv_alerts.yaml: alerts for sustained token cost regression (>20% sustained 10m relative to baseline), kv-miss rate increase (>5% absolute on high-volume routes), and KV op latency increase (p95 > 120ms).

Testing and validation: unit tests for new metric instrumentation and trace span tagging added; integration test that exercises caching hot-path; local Grafana dashboard validation via grafana-toolkit. Runbook updates included for SRE (observability/runbooks/token_kv_regression.md).

Rollout plan: feature rolled out behind feature flag obs.token_kv_tracing. Default off for Dedicated/private customers; enabled in staging and progressively in production over 48h while monitoring alerts. On first rollout we will keep alert thresholds conservative to avoid noisy pages; after 72h we'll re-evaluate thresholds and set final production values or enable auto-notify.

Notes: this PR intentionally avoids adding high-cardinality route+user labels to Prometheus metrics; where finer granularity was needed we expose per-route aggregated labels and rely on tracing to drill-to-request. The alert thresholds were chosen after a two-week lookback across historical metrics from prod and several benchmark workloads (ENG-2145).
